audit.whatIsWrong: content win[0..3] give Levels 1-4 to Ryze/Skill, but whys[0..3] in the same object say Aatrox out-trades an immobile Ryze at every one of those levels, and the packet level chart is Aatrox through First item. The chart contradicts its own reasons.
audit.why: Ryze has no dash and no self-peel before items; at 56.49% over 2202 games Aatrox is the early-lane favourite.
audit.corrected: Levels 1-4 belong to Aatrox; only Two+ items flips to Ryze.

audit.why: Spike table already keys off Lvl 3-5 kill window, Lvl 6 World Ender, first item, and full-build Ryze. Only the Realm Warp cooldown (180/160/140) was missing to make the Level 6 spike concrete.
audit.corrected: Added the 180s Realm Warp cooldown and the 9-11s Rune Prison cooldown to the spike text.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive ability interaction was never stated: Rune Prison (W) roots only if Spell Flux (E) is already on the target. Unmarked, it is a slow, which Umbral Dash and Aatrox's move speed shrug off.
audit.why: Riot's own text: 'Ryze traps a target in a cage of runes, damaging them and slowing their movement. If the target has Flux on it, they are instead rooted.' The order E-then-W is the entire lane.
audit.corrected: Step up while Spell Flux (E, 3.5s down to 2.5s) is spent, or accept the slow instead of the root; Rune Prison is back every 9-11s.

audit.whatIsWrong: No real cooldown numbers anywhere in the matchup.
audit.why: Rune Prison 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s and Realm Warp 180/160/140s are what make 'track his cooldown' actionable.
audit.corrected: Numbers added to mid and both early spikes.

edits.before: From level 3 you dominate — Ryze is immobile and squishy, and once you have W pull plus Q sweetspot you can lock him down. Pull him in, sweetspot-knockup, and drain through his Rune Prison root; if you dodge or tank one root he has no second peel tool. At 6 his Realm Warp is an escape, not combat stats, so your all-in stays strong — R, drain through the Overload poke, and delete him before his mana-shield sustain matters. Track that root cooldown obsessively.
edits.after: From level 3 you dominate — Ryze is immobile and squishy, and Infernal Chains into the third-Q knockup locks him down. Rune Prison only roots if Spell Flux (E) marked you first; unmarked it is a slow you walk through, so break that E-then-W order and he has no peel left. At 6 Realm Warp is a 180s repositioning portal, not combat stats, so pop R, drain the Overload poke, and delete him. Rune Prison returns every 9-11s.

edits.before: Your kill window — Ryze is squishy and immobile before items. Once you have Q pattern + W pull, close in: W-pull him, Q-sweetspot knockup, and E drain through his root (Rune Prison). If you dodge or eat one root, he has no way to peel you off.
edits.after: Your kill window — Ryze is squishy and immobile before items. Step up while Spell Flux (E) is spent: with no Flux mark on you, Rune Prison only slows. Chain him, third-Q knockup, E through it. Eat one root and he still has no way to peel you off.

edits.before: Ryze changes the lane by forcing Aatrox to respect Ryze root, phase/kiting tools, and scaling. Aatrox wins by controlling spacing with his first two Q swings, holding E until the enemy punish tool is committed, and managing the wave so the enemy must walk into the outer edge of his Q. Ryze wants to keep distance, poke Aatrox before he can reach the wave, and punish missed Qs with ranged damage or crowd control.
edits.after: Ryze changes the lane by forcing Aatrox to respect Rune Prison (W), which roots only once Spell Flux (E) has marked you and otherwise merely slows. Aatrox wins by spacing with the first two Darkin Blade swings, holding Umbral Dash until that root is spent, and dragging Ryze into Infernal Chains. Ryze wants distance, Overload poke every 5s, and the full build where he out-ranges every trade.
